question: As reported in the Italian news, an event featuring pro-Putin propaganda took place at Meucci High School in Aprilia before Christmas1. The event was organised by Openhub, a project that has received EU funding and has planned an exchange with Beregovoy High School in illegally-occupied Luhansk.

Involved in the organisation of the event was Andrea Lucidi, a pro-Putin journalist active in Donbas, and the association Vento dell’Est, chaired by Lorenzo Berti, a former member of the neofascist party CasaPound.

Vento dell’Est is know for pro-Kremlin propaganda activities in Italy, in particular the planning of an event in Lucca, Tuscany on 27 January 20242 in which Aleksander Dugin, known for his nationalist and revanchist ideology regarding Ukraine and for speaking out in favour of the Russian war of aggression3, was invited to participate via video-call. 1.
Against this backdrop, how can the Commission ensure that EU funds are not used for financing pro-Putin propaganda within the EU?
What action is the Commission planning to take to counter this dangerous tendency in Italy?
Supporter4
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.3.2024) 1.The programmes funded by the European Social Fund (ESF) are managed under the shared management principle. It is for the managing authority (MA) in charge of each programme to select projects, to follow up their implementation, and to verify the achievement of the results and the compliance with the conditions established in the grant agreement.
In all these steps the managing authority must ensure that the projects are in line with the programme objectives and with cohesion policy.

The Commission verifies that these activities are correctly performed via different monitoring and supervision mechanisms, including its participation in the Monitoring Committees and in the annual review meetings and annual performance reviews1, and its audits on the programme management and control system. If irregularities are detected, it can apply financial corrections.

In this specific case, according to available information, the initiative was organised by the consortium Openhub Lazio, which, following an open procedure, was awarded a grant under the Lazio 2014 - 2020 ESF operational programme for the creation of a network of ‘culturalsocial-work hubs’ in the region. The closure of the activities was scheduled for December 2023.

The checks on the execution, both on administrative and accounting nature and on the correct implementation of the interventions according to the approved project, will be carried out in the first quarter of 2024. 2.

The Commission will continue to perform its role in assessing how the MA ensures that the projects financed and their implementation are in line with the objectives of the programme and with cohesion policy.
1 Annual review meetings in the 2014-2020 period and annual performance reviews in the 2021-2027 one.
